/** Select a fixture mode only while the production driver captures its immutable setting. */
internal fun <T> withRun1MarkMode(mode: MarkMode, body: () -> T): T {
    val property = "opentaint.bidi.run1MarkMode"
    val previous = System.getProperty(property)
    try {
        System.setProperty(property, mode.name)
        return body()
    } finally {
        if (previous == null) System.clearProperty(property) else System.setProperty(property, previous)
    }
}

data class ProgramCase(val root: MethodKey, val rule: RuleId, val sink: CommonInst, val source: PathEdge)
data class DriverInput(val run: Int, val callee: MethodKey, val link: Link)
data class DriverProcessed(val run: Int, val method: MethodKey, val delta: EdgeDelta)
data class DemandLinkCase(val root: MethodKey, val sourceMethod: MethodKey, val reader: MethodKey,
                          val sinkMethod: MethodKey, val rule: RuleId, val sink: CommonInst,
                          val source: PathEdge, val q: Int, val r: Int, val g: Int, val h: Int,
                          val mark: TaintMark)

/** Joined engine results are retained here only as explicit test observations. */
class DriverFixtures(threads: Int = 1) : AutoCloseable {
    val program = FiniteProgramFixtures(threads = threads)
    val shared get() = program.shared
    val manager get() = program.manager
    val ops get() = program.ops
    val records get() = program.records
    val vulnerabilities get() = program.vulnerabilities
    val cancellation get() = program.cancellation
    val refManager get() = program.refManager
    val configs = ArrayList<RunConfig>()
    val results = ArrayList<RunResult<RunMethodAnalyzer>>()
    val timeouts = ArrayList<Duration>()
    private val processRows = ConcurrentLinkedQueue<DriverProcessed>()
    private val inputRows = ConcurrentLinkedQueue<DriverInput>()
    fun links(run: Int, method: MethodKey): List<Link> = inputRows.filter { it.run == run && it.callee == method }.map { it.link }.distinct()
    val processed: List<DriverProcessed> get() = processRows.toList()

    fun manager(config: RunConfig, owner: SharedObjects = shared): RunManager<RunMethodAnalyzer> {
        val actual = RunMethodHandlers(MethodLocalServicesFactory(::RunMethodLocalServices),
            MethodCallServicesFactory(::RunMethodCallServices))
        val factory = RunnerHandlerFactory<RunMethodAnalyzer> { port ->
            val observed = object : RunnerPort<RunMethodAnalyzer> by port {
                // Restricted input stays in the caller. Observe eligible bindings
                // at subscription, not at the now-key-only callee packet.
                override fun subscribe(sub: Subscription) {
                    if (config.restricted && !sub.zeroOnly) ops.leaves(sub.added).forEach {
                        inputRows += DriverInput(config.index, sub.callee, Link(it, sub.linkLayer, sub.ref))
                    }
                    port.subscribe(sub)
                }
                override fun link(callee: MethodKey, ref: CallerRef, linkLayer: Layer, added: Facts) {
                    ops.leaves(added).forEach { inputRows += DriverInput(config.index, callee, Link(it, linkLayer, ref)) }
                    port.link(callee, ref, linkLayer, added)
                }
                override val onProcess: (MethodKey, EdgeDelta) -> Unit = { key, delta ->
                    processRows += DriverProcessed(config.index, key, delta)
                    port.onProcess?.invoke(key, delta)
                }
            }
            actual.create(observed)
        }
        return RunManager(config, owner, factory, quantum = 1)
    }

    fun run(config: RunConfig, owner: SharedObjects = shared,
            timeout: Duration = 5.seconds): RunResult<RunMethodAnalyzer> {
        configs += config
        timeouts += timeout
        return manager(config, owner).run(timeout).also(results::add)
    }

    fun driver(policy: IterationPolicy, budget: Duration = 5.seconds,
               invokeRun: (RunConfig, SharedObjects, Duration) -> RunResult<RunMethodAnalyzer> = this::run,
               run1MarkMode: MarkMode? = null,
               guardBarrier: (SharedObjects, () -> Next) -> Next = { _, body -> body() }): IterationDriver =
        if (run1MarkMode == null) IterationDriver(policy, shared, budget, invokeRun, guardBarrier)
        else withRun1MarkMode(run1MarkMode) { IterationDriver(policy, shared, budget, invokeRun, guardBarrier) }

    fun rule(id: String): RuleId = object : CommonTaintConfigurationSink {
        override val id = id
        override val meta = object : CommonTaintConfigurationSinkMeta {
            override val message = id
            override val severity = CommonTaintConfigurationSinkMeta.Severity.Warning
        }
    }

    fun summary(vararg edges: PathEdge): StatementSummary =
        StatementSummary(edges.map { it.from.base }.toSet(), edges.map(MicroEdge::of), emptyList(), emptyMap())

    private fun sourceRules(edge: PathEdge): RuleStatement =
        RuleStatement(summary(ZERO_KEEP, edge), StatementSummary.EMPTY, emptyList())

    private fun exitSink(sink: SinkRule): ExitRules =
        ExitRules(RuleStatement(StatementSummary.EMPTY, StatementSummary.EMPTY, listOf(sink)), false, emptySet())

    /** A normal root witness remains an unproved candidate under the minimal report policy. */
    fun confirmed(): ProgramCase {
        val root = program.method("confirmed", listOf(listOf(1), emptyList()), 1).key()
        val mark = MarkSlot.Concrete(program.mark("confirmed T"))
        val base = AccessPathBase.LocalVar(0)
        val source = PathEdge(ZERO_FACT, PathFact(base, emptyList(), Tail.EXACT, mark), ExclusionSet.Empty)
        val sink = SinkRule(rule("confirmed sink"), 0, listOf(program.pattern(base, mark = mark)), emptyList())
        program.entry(root, sourceRules(source))
        program.exit(root, 1, exitSink(sink))
        return ProgramCase(root, sink.rule, program.inst(root, 1), source)
    }

    /** The explicit may pass keeps this finding unconfirmed at every field limit. */
    fun persistentDemand(): ProgramCase {
        val root = program.method("persistent demand", listOf(listOf(1), listOf(2), emptyList()), 2).key()
        val mark = MarkSlot.Concrete(program.mark("persistent T"))
        val base = AccessPathBase.LocalVar(0)
        val source = PathEdge(ZERO_FACT, PathFact(base, emptyList(), Tail.EXACT, mark), ExclusionSet.Empty)
        val may = PathEdge(source.to, PathFact(AccessPathBase.Return, emptyList(), Tail.ANY, mark), ExclusionSet.Empty)
        val sink = SinkRule(rule("persistent sink"), 0,
            listOf(program.pattern(AccessPathBase.Return, tail = Tail.ANY, mark = mark)), emptyList())
        program.entry(root, sourceRules(source))
        program.statement(root, 1, summary(may))
        program.exit(root, 2, exitSink(sink))
        return ProgramCase(root, sink.rule, program.inst(root, 2), source)
    }

    /** A longer exact source is cut in run 1 and recovered by a real backward source hit. */
    fun refining(): ProgramCase {
        val root = program.method("refining", listOf(listOf(1), emptyList()), 1).key()
        val mark = MarkSlot.Concrete(program.mark("refining T"))
        val path = listOf(program.field("a"), program.field("b"))
        val source = PathEdge(ZERO_FACT, PathFact(AccessPathBase.Return, path, Tail.EXACT, mark), ExclusionSet.Empty)
        val sink = SinkRule(rule("refining sink"), 0, listOf(Pattern(source.to, ExclusionSet.Empty)), emptyList())
        program.entry(root, sourceRules(source))
        program.exit(root, 1, exitSink(sink))
        return ProgramCase(root, sink.rule, program.inst(root, 1), source)
    }

    /** Two different normal call sites cannot jointly support one callee conjunction. */
    fun unsupportedJoint(): ProgramCase {
        val root = program.method("separate sites", listOf(listOf(1), listOf(2), listOf(3), emptyList()), 3).key()
        val callee = program.method("joint sink", listOf(listOf(1), emptyList()), 1).key()
        val first = AccessPathBase.LocalVar(0)
        val second = AccessPathBase.LocalVar(1)
        val arg0 = AccessPathBase.Argument(0)
        val arg1 = AccessPathBase.Argument(1)
        val t = MarkSlot.Concrete(program.mark("joint T"))
        val u = MarkSlot.Concrete(program.mark("joint U"))
        val source = PathEdge(ZERO_FACT, PathFact(first, emptyList(), Tail.EXACT, t), ExclusionSet.Empty)
        val other = PathEdge(ZERO_FACT, PathFact(second, emptyList(), Tail.EXACT, u), ExclusionSet.Empty)
        val sink = SinkRule(rule("unsupported joint sink"), 0,
            listOf(program.pattern(arg0, mark = t), program.pattern(arg1, mark = u)), emptyList())
        program.entry(root, RuleStatement(summary(ZERO_KEEP, source, other), StatementSummary.EMPTY, emptyList()))
        fun call(value: AccessPathBase, argument: AccessPathBase) = CallPlan(setOf(value), listOf(
            CallStage.Edges(BEFORE, BOUND, BIND_IN, summary(starEdge(value, emptyList(), argument, emptyList()), ZERO_KEEP)),
            CallStage.Actions(BOUND, ADDED, emptyList()),
            CallStage.Callees(ADDED, RETURNED, listOf(callee)),
            CallStage.Actions(RETURNED, REWRITTEN, emptyList()),
            CallStage.Edges(REWRITTEN, AFTER, BIND_BACK, summary(ZERO_KEEP)),
        ), emptyList(), BEFORE, AFTER)
        program.call(root, 1, call(first, arg0))
        program.call(root, 2, call(second, arg1))
        program.exit(callee, 1, exitSink(sink))
        return ProgramCase(root, sink.rule, program.inst(callee, 1), source)
    }

    /** DLINK: srcAny; c(x) reads q then r; m cleans its root EXACT before the g.h sink and throws. */
    fun demandLink(): DemandLinkCase {
        val root = program.method("dlink root", listOf(listOf(1), listOf(2), listOf(3), emptyList()), 3).key()
        val sourceMethod = program.method("dlink srcAny", listOf(listOf(1), emptyList()), 1).key()
        val reader = program.method("dlink c", listOf(listOf(1), listOf(2), listOf(3), listOf(4), emptyList()), 4).key()
        // The normal exit is unreachable. Reached requirements and the sink flow through the exceptional exit.
        val sinkMethod = program.method("dlink m", listOf(listOf(1), listOf(2), emptyList(), emptyList()),
            normalExit = 3, exceptionalExit = 2).key()
        val dto = AccessPathBase.LocalVar(0)
        val temporary = AccessPathBase.LocalVar(1)
        val value = AccessPathBase.LocalVar(2)
        val argument = AccessPathBase.Argument(0)
        val returned = AccessPathBase.Return
        val q = program.field("q")
        val r = program.field("r")
        val g = program.field("g")
        val h = program.field("h")
        val taint = program.mark("DLINK T")
        val mark = MarkSlot.Concrete(taint)
        val source = PathEdge(ZERO_FACT, PathFact(returned, emptyList(), Tail.ANY_TAINT, mark), ExclusionSet.Empty)
        program.entry(sourceMethod, sourceRules(source))
        fun resolved(callee: MethodKey, bindIn: StatementSummary, bindBack: StatementSummary,
                     touched: Set<AccessPathBase>, cleaner: Cleaner? = null): CallPlan = CallPlan(touched, listOf(
            CallStage.Edges(BEFORE, BOUND, BIND_IN, bindIn),
            CallStage.Actions(BOUND, ADDED, cleaner?.let { listOf(CleanStep.Clean(it)) }.orEmpty()),
            CallStage.Callees(ADDED, RETURNED, listOf(callee)),
            CallStage.Actions(RETURNED, REWRITTEN, emptyList()),
            CallStage.Edges(REWRITTEN, AFTER, BIND_BACK, bindBack),
        ), emptyList(), BEFORE, AFTER)
        program.call(root, 1, resolved(sourceMethod, summary(ZERO_KEEP),
            summary(starEdge(returned, emptyList(), dto, emptyList()), ZERO_KEEP), setOf(dto)))
        program.call(root, 2, resolved(reader, summary(starEdge(dto, emptyList(), argument, emptyList()), ZERO_KEEP),
            summary(ZERO_KEEP), setOf(dto)))
        program.statement(reader, 1, StatementSummary(setOf(argument, temporary),
            listOf(MicroEdge.of(keepEdge(argument)), MicroEdge.of(starEdge(argument, listOf(q), temporary, emptyList()))),
            emptyList(), emptyMap()))
        program.statement(reader, 2, StatementSummary(setOf(temporary, value),
            listOf(MicroEdge.of(keepEdge(temporary)), MicroEdge.of(starEdge(temporary, listOf(r), value, emptyList()))),
            emptyList(), emptyMap()))
        program.call(reader, 3, resolved(sinkMethod, summary(starEdge(value, emptyList(), argument, emptyList()), ZERO_KEEP),
            summary(ZERO_KEEP), setOf(value), Cleaner(argument, null, CleanReach.EXACT, taint)))
        val sink = SinkRule(rule("DLINK sink"), 0, listOf(program.pattern(argument, listOf(g, h), mark = mark)), emptyList())
        program.call(sinkMethod, 1, CallPlan(setOf(argument), listOf(
            CallStage.Edges(BEFORE, BOUND, BIND_IN, summary(keepEdge(argument), ZERO_KEEP)),
            CallStage.Actions(BOUND, ADDED, emptyList()),
            CallStage.Edges(ADDED, RETURNED, UNRESOLVED, summary(keepEdge(argument), ZERO_KEEP)),
            CallStage.Actions(RETURNED, REWRITTEN, emptyList()),
            CallStage.Edges(REWRITTEN, AFTER, BIND_BACK, summary(keepEdge(argument), ZERO_KEEP)),
        ), listOf(sink), BEFORE, AFTER))
        return DemandLinkCase(root, sourceMethod, reader, sinkMethod, sink.rule, program.inst(sinkMethod, 1),
            source, q, r, g, h, taint)
    }

    override fun close(): Unit = program.close()
}

/** Real shell services over a small, fixed common IR graph. */
class EngineShellFixtures(val cancellation: Cancellation = Cancellation(),
                          markDeclarations: MarkDeclarations = COMMON_FIXTURE_DECLARATIONS) {
    data class Context(val name: String) : MethodContext
    data class Unit(val name: String) : UnitType

    private class Method(override val name: String) : CommonMethod {
        override val parameters: List<CommonMethodParameter> = emptyList()
        override val returnType = object : CommonTypeName { override val typeName = "java.lang.Object" }
        override fun flowGraph(): ControlFlowGraph<CommonInst> = error("The fixture supplies its compact graph")
        override fun toString(): String = name
    }

    val methodA: CommonMethod = Method("methodA")
    val methodB: CommonMethod = Method("methodB")
    val methodUnknown: CommonMethod = Method("methodUnknown")
    val unitA: UnitType = Unit("A")
    val unitB: UnitType = Unit("B")
    val unitResolver = UnitResolver<CommonMethod> { method -> when (method) {
        methodA -> unitA
        methodB -> unitB
        else -> UnknownUnit
    } }

    val refManager = RefManager()
    val manager = testApManager(cancellation, refManager, markDeclarations)
    val ops = ApOps(manager)
    val records = PersistentRecordStore(manager)
    val vulnerabilities = ConcurrentVulnerabilityStore(manager)
    private val instructions = ConcurrentHashMap<Pair<CommonMethod, Int>, CommonInst>()
    private val graphs = ConcurrentHashMap<Pair<CommonMethod, Direction>, MethodInstGraph>()
    private val forms = ConcurrentHashMap<MethodKey, MethodForms>()
    val callExpr = object : CommonCallExpr {
        override val typeName = "java.lang.Object"
        override val args: List<CommonValue> = emptyList()
    }

    fun inst(method: CommonMethod, index: Int): CommonInst {
        require(index in 0..4)
        return instructions.computeIfAbsent(method to index) { object : CommonInst {
            override val location = object : CommonInstLocation {
                override val method = method
                override val index = index
            }
            override fun toString(): String = "${method.name}:$index"
        } }
    }

    fun key(method: CommonMethod = methodA, context: String = "context", entry: Int = 0): MethodKey =
        MethodKey(Context(context), inst(method, entry))

    val a: MethodKey = key(methodA)
    val b: MethodKey = key(methodB)
    val unknown: MethodKey = key(methodUnknown)

    val language = object : LanguageManager {
        override fun getInstIndex(inst: CommonInst): Int = inst.location.index
        override fun getMaxInstIndex(method: CommonMethod): Int = 4
        override fun getInstByIndex(method: CommonMethod, index: Int): CommonInst = inst(method, index)
        override fun isEmpty(method: CommonMethod): Boolean = false
        override fun getCallExpr(inst: CommonInst): CommonCallExpr? = callExpr.takeIf { inst.location.index == 2 }
        override fun producesExceptionalControlFlow(inst: CommonInst): Boolean = inst.location.index == 2
        override fun getCalleeMethod(callExpr: CommonCallExpr): CommonMethod = methodB
        override val methodContextSerializer: MethodContextSerializer get() = error("Unused by shell tests")
    }

    fun graph(method: CommonMethod, direction: Direction): MethodInstGraph = graphs.computeIfAbsent(method to direction) {
        val successors = if (direction == Direction.FORWARD)
            listOf(listOf(1), listOf(2), listOf(3, 4), emptyList(), emptyList())
        else listOf(emptyList(), listOf(0), listOf(1), listOf(2), listOf(2))
        val compact = CompactGraph.build(5) { index -> BitSet().apply { successors[index].forEach(::set) } }
        val exits = BitSet().apply {
            if (direction == Direction.FORWARD) { set(3); set(4) } else set(0)
        }
        MethodInstGraph(Array(5) { inst(method, it) }, compact, exits)
    }

    fun methodForms(key: MethodKey): MethodForms = forms.computeIfAbsent(key) {
        val statement = StatementSummary(setOf(AccessPathBase.Argument(0)),
            listOf(MicroEdge.of(starEdge(AccessPathBase.Argument(0), emptyList(), AccessPathBase.Return, emptyList()))),
            emptyList(), emptyMap())
        val backwardStatement = statement.reversed()
        val entry = RuleStatement(StatementSummary.identities(listOf(AccessPathBase.Zero, AccessPathBase.Argument(0))),
            StatementSummary.EMPTY, emptyList())
        val backwardEntry = entry.reversed()
        val forwardExit = ExitRules(entry, globalStateDrop = true, entryMarks = setOf(manager.marks.mark("entry")))
        val backwardExit = ExitRules(forwardExit.reversed(), false, emptySet())
        val forwardCall = CallPlan(setOf(AccessPathBase.Argument(0), AccessPathBase.Return),
            listOf(CallStage.Edges(CallPoint.BEFORE, CallPoint.AFTER, StageKind.PASS_OVER, statement)),
            emptyList(), CallPoint.BEFORE, CallPoint.AFTER)
        val backwardCall = forwardCall.reversed()
        object : MethodForms {
            override fun statement(direction: Direction, s: CommonInst): StatementSummary =
                if (direction == Direction.FORWARD) statement else backwardStatement
            override fun call(direction: Direction, s: CommonInst, call: CommonCallExpr): CallPlan =
                if (direction == Direction.FORWARD) forwardCall else backwardCall
            override fun entryRules(direction: Direction): RuleStatement =
                if (direction == Direction.FORWARD) entry else backwardEntry
            override fun exitRules(direction: Direction, exit: CommonInst): ExitRules =
                if (direction == Direction.FORWARD) forwardExit else backwardExit
        }
    }

    val interpreter = object : Interpreter {
        override fun entryNode(method: MethodKey): CommonInst = method.statement
        override fun exitNodes(method: MethodKey): List<ExitNode> =
            listOf(ExitNode(inst(method.method, 3), false), ExitNode(inst(method.method, 4), true))
        override fun entryRules(method: MethodKey): RuleStatement = methodForms(method).entryRules(Direction.FORWARD)
        override fun exitRules(method: MethodKey, exit: CommonInst): ExitRules =
            methodForms(method).exitRules(Direction.FORWARD, exit)
        override fun statementSummary(method: MethodKey, statement: CommonInst): StatementSummary =
            methodForms(method).statement(Direction.FORWARD, statement)
        override fun callPlan(caller: MethodKey, statement: CommonInst, call: CommonCallExpr): CallPlan =
            methodForms(caller).call(Direction.FORWARD, statement, call)
        override fun isSummaryBase(base: AccessPathBase): Boolean =
            base !is AccessPathBase.LocalVar && base !is AccessPathBase.CleanerTemporary
    }
    val contexts = MethodContextCache(interpreter, object : MethodContextSource {
        override fun forms(key: MethodKey): MethodForms = methodForms(key)
        override fun graph(key: MethodKey, direction: Direction): MethodInstGraph = graph(key.method, direction)
    })

    fun shared(threads: Int = 1, unitResolver: UnitResolver<CommonMethod> = this.unitResolver,
               cancellationTimeout: Duration = 1.seconds, diagnostics: Boolean = false): SharedObjects =
        SharedObjects(manager, ops, interpreter, language, contexts, records, unitResolver,
            refManager, cancellation, threads, cancellationTimeout, diagnostics)

    fun config(index: Int = 1, L: Int = maxOf(1, index - 1), roots: List<MethodKey> = listOf(a),
               demand: DemandStore? = if (index == 1) null else DemandStore.Builder(manager).build(),
               seeds: SeedIndex = SeedIndex.EMPTY): RunConfig =
        RunConfig(index, L, demand, records.view(), seeds, roots)

    fun field(name: String): Int = manager.accessors.index(FieldAccessor("Box", name, "Box"))
    fun pattern(base: AccessPathBase = AccessPathBase.Argument(0), path: List<Int> = emptyList(),
                tail: Tail = Tail.EXACT, mark: MarkSlot = MarkSlot.Concrete(manager.marks.mark("T")),
                exclusion: ExclusionSet = ExclusionSet.Empty): Pattern = Pattern(PathFact(base, path, tail, mark), exclusion)
    fun fact(base: AccessPathBase = AccessPathBase.Argument(0), path: List<Int> = emptyList(),
             tail: Tail = Tail.EXACT, mark: MarkSlot = MarkSlot.Concrete(manager.marks.mark("T")),
             exclusion: ExclusionSet = ExclusionSet.Empty, layer: Layer = Layer.NORMAL): Facts =
        manager.factsOf(PathFact(base, path, tail, mark), exclusion, layer)
}

/** Frozen a80 summary/request protocol law fixture; no selected-engine claim. */
class HistoricalPipelineFixtures(index: Int = 1, limit: Int = 3,
                       val protocol: ProtocolSteps = ProtocolSteps.Inline) : AutoCloseable {
    val method = MethodAnalysisFixtures()
    val store = method.store
    val ap = method.manager
    val ops = method.ops
    val caller = method.key
    val callee = store.key(context = "callee")
    val records = method.records
    val config = method.config(index = index, L = limit)
    val storages = LinkedHashMap<MethodKey, SummaryStorage>()
    val staticFootprints = LinkedHashMap<CommonMethod, Run1StaticFootprint>()
    val deliveries = ArrayList<RunEvent.Delivery>()
    data class Summary(val caller: MethodKey, val part: Subscription, val publication: Publication, val member: Int)
    data class Native(val caller: MethodKey, val part: Subscription, val record: Record)
    data class View(val caller: MethodKey, val part: Subscription, val view: RecordLeafView, val nonSubsumable: Boolean = false)
    val summaries = ArrayList<Summary>()
    val native = ArrayList<Native>()
    val views = ArrayList<View>()
    var onSummary: ((Summary) -> Unit)? = null
    var onRecord: ((Native) -> Unit)? = null
    var onView: ((View) -> Unit)? = null
    var onPost: ((RunEvent.Delivery) -> Unit)? = null

    fun storage(key: MethodKey = callee): SummaryStorage = storages.getOrPut(key) {
        SummaryStorage(key, ap, ops, protocol)
    }

    val port = object : SubscriptionPort {
        override val config get() = this@HistoricalPipelineFixtures.config
        override val ops get() = this@HistoricalPipelineFixtures.ops
        override val steps get() = protocol
        override fun summaryStorage(key: MethodKey): SummaryStorage = storage(key)
        override fun staticFootprint(method: CommonMethod): Run1StaticFootprint? = staticFootprints[method]
        override fun applier(caller: MethodKey): SummaryApplier = object : SummaryApplier {
            override fun applySummary(part: Subscription, pub: Publication, member: Int) {
                val application = Summary(caller, part, pub, member)
                summaries += application
                onSummary?.invoke(application)
            }
            override fun applyRecord(part: Subscription, record: Record) {
                val application = Native(caller, part, record)
                native += application
                onRecord?.invoke(application)
            }
            override fun applyRecordView(part: Subscription, view: RecordLeafView, nonSubsumable: Boolean) {
                val application = View(caller, part, view, nonSubsumable)
                views += application
                onView?.invoke(application)
            }
        }
        override fun post(event: RunEvent.Delivery): Boolean {
            deliveries += event
            onPost?.invoke(event)
            return true
        }
    }
    val subscriptions = SubscriptionManager(port)

    fun subscription(added: Facts = store.fact(), premise: PremiseKey =
        if (added is FlowTree) ops.policy(added) else ap.zero,
                     callerLayer: Layer = Layer.NORMAL, call: Int = 1,
                     caller: MethodKey = this.caller, callee: MethodKey = this.callee,
                     zeroOnly: Boolean = false): Subscription =
        Subscription(callee, CallerRef(caller, premise, callerLayer, store.inst(call)), added.layer, added, zeroOnly)

    fun deliverAll() {
        while (deliveries.isNotEmpty()) {
            val event = deliveries.removeAt(0)
            subscriptions.onDelivery(event.callee, event.publications)
        }
    }

    override fun close() { subscriptions.freeze(); method.close() }
}

    val keys = linkedMapOf<String, FullKey>()

    val flags = linkedMapOf<MarkGroupKey, Boolean>()

}

# Access paths and storages — specification

Next-iteration summary restriction is specified in
[Demand-relative summary restriction](demand-relative-summary-restriction.md).
It selects exact paired C5 followed by an exit-relative field cut and
admitted-only summary storage/persistence for both layers. It is a design
target; the runtime remains unchanged. Its scope does not change C2 or the
selected typed Target protocol.

Selected restricted-call integration: use the
[implementation contract](../docs/design/bidirectional-selected-call-policy-implementation-20261030.md).
The caller applies persisted records on every original offer before current
demand admission. It runs the complete existing initial-emission operation;
only a nonempty result permits current subscription and replay. It sends
final canonical keys to the callee, which only starts unseen keys. Keep the
AP emission, matching, C5, record and transfer tables unchanged. This policy
does not use applicability of a hypothetical normalized summary as admission.


> The selected 22 October
> [local-writer and summary-alias contract](run1-static-writers-and-summary-aliases.md)
> overrides run-1 static writer registration and forward alias admission
> below. Call summaries promote without new writer registration. Computed
> supplies remain. The scalar no-memory-effect rule has no DEMAND bypass.
> Other AP, field, source, demand and later-run contracts do not change.

> The selected 21 October all-origin rule in §0.4 replaces the earlier
> representative rule. After a complete compatible run-1 binding, emit each
> contributing nonzero origin as a separate atomic edge. Emit ZERO only for a
> complete permitted all-ZERO binding. Later FULL runs keep exact ND rules.
> This is a semantic correction; routing/projection edits preserve its behavior.

> For the selected mark/static change, use [Mark groups and direct static handling](grouped-run1-statics.md)
> and its pinned pre-bottom-up baseline. It overrides older proposal links
> at the listed phase seams. Other ordinary contracts below remain in force.
> This specification work does not change the runtime.

The selected [rule-group mark contract](rule-group-marks.md) takes precedence
for mark ownership, run-1 group values, selected-mark cleaners, typed mark
exclusions, group requests and the run schedule. Run-1 is FORWARD/group/limit
1; run-2 is BACKWARD/full/limit 1. This is a specification change; the analyzer
implementation is unchanged. Its [proof dossier](rule-group-mark-proofs.md)
states the checked scope and the remaining runtime adapter obligations.

The [unified run-1 contract](run1-field-writes.md) has precedence for static
field/mark requests, initial emission/replay, selective field writes, Empty-E
producers, ordinary static defaults and later strong refinement.
Complete overwrite kills and disjoint preservation stay ordinary. Only a
surviving residual needing a field-exclusion update demotes, with Empty E.
Every run-1 intermediate field exclusion is Empty. Default static identities use ordinary summary
storage/application and the closed StaticMayWrite bit; no root initial is
emitted in F1. Demotion changes only the edge layer, preserving the complete
AP and tail. It overrides older W2/W8 layer-driven conversions to ANY below.
Later strong E semantics remain. [New proofs](run1-field-write-proofs.md) state the exact scope.

The same [unified contract](run1-field-writes.md) takes precedence
over the static rules below: separate value-read/mark gates, nine run-1
initial families, exclusion-update demotion and ordinary stored defaults, guidance-only
run-1 export, and actual-query strong run-2/later analysis. It is a design
target; runtime is unchanged. [Static proofs](static-handling-proofs.md)
state the new laws and the local checked scope. Historical root/frame
theorems retain their original assumptions.

This document defines facts, edges, AP operations, runs, and stores for
[bidirectional-task.md](../bidirectional-task.md). It is normative.

The selected [correlated concrete initial extension](run1-correlated-concrete-initials.md)
replaces the concrete-STAR ban in W2: a concrete STAR initial starts with a
correlated concrete STAR DEMAND conclusion in every run and mark mode. It
also makes FLOW subsumption a general mechanism in both directions, with
explicit geometry, exclusion, layer and protection gates. It lists the
remaining ANY producers. The extension is implemented and takes precedence
for these cells. Historical W2 proofs keep their original assumptions.
The detailed implementation proposal also selects persistence of NORMAL FLOW
with nonempty initial/output exclusions and proves identity-only alias
redundancy under semantic input alias closure. Its
[implementation proof dossier](correlated-concrete-implementation-proofs.md)
states the reference invariants. The
[local validation report](../docs/reports/bidirectional-correlated-concrete-validation-20261026.md)
records the Kotlin correspondence checks; fresh project validation remains pending.

[interpreter.md](interpreter.md) defines IR construction and rule order.
[analyzer-core.md](analyzer-core.md) defines events, ownership, scheduling, and the
iteration driver. Each rule has one owner; the other specs use its contract.

The current rules include F72 demand sharing, F74 field-cleaner lowering, F75
base-dependent cleaner splitting, F76 must-summary read views, F77 structural
summary demand selection, and F78 mark-only run-1 requests with static frame composition. [ap-history.md](ap-history.md) records the decisions.
[proof-status.md](proof-status.md) separates current checked results from historical
proofs and open obligations. Local proof results do not establish the full current
iteration. A Lean name is evidence; the rules and their conditions are stated here.

F78 is specified in [run1-requests.md](run1-requests.md). It takes precedence for
run-1 request keys, static planning, emission, root-summary composition and request
ownership. [run1-request-proofs.md](run1-request-proofs.md) states the constructive
proofs and their limits. This is a normative target; measured runtime
`27e22bb1ed871651143538783473cb0d4fcbcf3e` is unchanged. No callee AddedFactStore,
full-query/role question table, or deferred concrete-answer memo is required. Caller
N2 inputs remain. Earlier scalar request/static results keep their historical scope.

Language: ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English.

---

## 0. Scope

This spec defines:

* the fact representation for the forward and the backward analysis;
* the operations on facts: delta-concat, micro edge application, summary edge application, summary restriction, field
  limit, mark gate and mark request, mark conjunction (ND edges), cleaner, type filter, emission, reversal;
* the storages that the analyzer uses in one run and across runs;
* the soundness theorems for these operations and the scope in which they hold.

This spec does not define the IR interpretation (`interpreter.md`), the analyzer scheduling, the iteration driver (§6.6
gives only its general requirement and its stop rules; `analyzer-core.md` §7 defines the driver) or the trace
resolution (out of scope; §8.10 gives the traces of the report). It defines the contracts that these parts use. The
contract of the backward run (contract B) is in §6.6.

### 0.1 Construction and proof conditions

These conditions are part of the design. The interpreter and analyzer must enforce
them. Each proof uses only the conditions stated in [proof-status.md](proof-status.md).

| # | Condition | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | Statement summaries list touched bases and all micro edges. Each micro edge describes exactly its flow in §3.5. The reference semantics first performs the signed folds of `interpreter.md` §4.2, then treats residual negative mark literals as true. A pass rule has no mark literal; a pass rule with such a literal is the over-approximation of §11.1. Other rule errors reject the whole rule. | Interpreter |
| S2 | Alias gen edges describe aliases that can hold. Alias writes are weak: an alias base is not touched and keeps its content. The formal reference program is alias-free. | Alias analysis |
| S3 | A method does not reassign formal parameters. | IR |
| S4 | Each exit kind has one exit. Normal and exceptional exits form one virtual exit: end rules and backward starts act at both; only the normal exit produces summaries. | CFG |
| S5 | A type filter is prefix-closed and accepts every path that a real value of its static type can have (§4.8). | Type checker |
| S6 | A complete run is the least fixed point of §6.1. Worklist order does not change that result. | Analyzer |
| S7 | No micro edge or binding has a `*∖X` premise. A concrete target mark requires a concrete premise mark. | Interpreter |
| S8 | No initial fact, micro edge, or binding has `*/Universe`. A `$` premise has a concrete mark. No micro edge has a `$` premise and `*` target; a `$` target requires a concrete premise mark. | Interpreter |
| S9 | Each conjunction literal names a concrete mark. | Interpreter |
| S10 | A statement edge reads a touched base. Every call binding has `*` premise mark and `*` tails on both sides. A conjunctive target has a concrete mark and no `*` tail (W7). | Interpreter |
| S11 | Backward construction: (a) binding target marks are `*`; (b) statement edges are mark-reversible (§1); (c) no forward back-binding targets zero; (d) each non-call keeps zero, no cleaner acts on zero, and a filter on zero accepts its empty path; (e) each node reachable from a root/callee entry can reach its virtual exit; (f) sink patterns have `$` or `[any]`; (g) statement edges and bindings have exact shape (§1): a `*` premise with a `$` or `[any]` target has empty field exclusion. Clause (g) is needed for generic reversed-edge exactness; the record views of §8.7 have their own shapes. | Interpreter and CFG |
| S12 | Static construction: a static position is a read/sink path on `S`, cut to the class and field. An `S→S` edge is an identity restriction or reads and writes at/below a static field. An edge from another base to a bare class position has concrete `$` premise and target; each literal of a conjunctive edge has the same form. No pass rule reads/writes a bare class position. Calls bind `S.*→S.*`. Class accessors do not count. F78 selects run-1 limit exactly 1; later limits are positive and nondecreasing. A cleaner on `S` names its mark; removing all marks at a static position is a strong-write kill. The empty-path whole-base all-mark cleaner is the one exception: it drops each `S` fact whole. `S` differs from zero. Run 1 uses §6.2 and its bounded-input grammar. Restricted runs require the edge/binding/limit conditions and records that preserve the static invariant. | Interpreter |
| S13 | Validity for exactness: filters accept all valid locations; validity of an edge's end implies validity of its start, for statement edges and both call bindings. For conjunctions this holds for each literal. | Type-filter placement |
| S14 | Input records are exact on valid end locations. Must records are end-exact on admitted locations, have concrete conclusions, and satisfy W8 normal form. Reversed backward records require the extra conditions of §8.7; dropping backward filters can break exactness (§11.1). | Record store |
| S15 | Only sources and triggered end-fact actions use a `[any-taint]` target, with concrete premise/target marks. Pass rules with an AnyField target use may `[any]`; AnyField pass premises are rejected. No micro edge has a `[any-taint]` premise. The backward run has no `[any-taint]`; reversing a may target puts every result in the demand layer. | Interpreter |
| S16 | A field cleaner uses an action-scoped temporary (a deterministic key for a generated action; a fresh token for manual construction): read the field, clean the temporary root, strongly write it back. Keep the read identity and strong-write keep edges. Reverse all three steps backward. The temporary does not escape or enter a summary (§4.7). | Interpreter |

The current demand contract also requires normalized patterns and the explicit
entry-tail guard in §6.1. This guard is proved for the alternating base model; its
full X-tail and pipeline construction is open. Claims about soundness of every
current iteration remain proof obligations (§11.2).

---

### 0.2 Bound NNF rule contracts and cache independence

`interpreter.md` §4.2 defines signed folding before/after static evaluation and residual negative projection.
Production source/sink conditions use one owned NNF DAG per stable bound occurrence, not a DNF/action/array
product. FALSE has no AP effect or positive footprint. Keep non-false positive reads such as B in
`A OR (A AND B)`; a later root firing is not a prerequisite for its leaf read/drop effect.

Unary source uses execute the ordinary §4.1 transfer on the incoming facts. Multi uses execute §4.6 mark checks
and target construction. One canonical leaf can belong to both classes; repeated bindings must agree. Proof scope
and complete premise/layer/group headers keep observed alternatives separate. Growing matched facts emit their
new versions under the same structural proof. These are required implementation equivalence conditions, not a new
soundness or iteration theorem. The existing AP tables, exclusions, F74 cuts, F75 dispatch and F76/F77 rules remain.

Managed form reclamation must change only allocation addresses and build counts. Stable rule/action/temporary
keys and callback pins preserve effects. Actor support records and persistent witnesses retain owned descriptors,
not compiled graphs or form caches. See `interpreter.md` §0.2 and `analyzer-core.md` §4.8 for the owner lifetimes.

### 0.3 Input history and runtime storage

A semantic history of admitted inputs/links is ghost state, not a callee runtime store.
Caller N2 retains actual input Facts and full provenance (§8.4). The callee consumes each
transport payload and releases it. Under F78 its request state is one owner-write-only
pending RequestStorage P; SummaryStorage owns the one cumulative RequestStorage R.
Both use the same class. R borrows the closed plan's immutable precomputed base B
and keeps only disjoint dynamic residual D; P has an empty base. No seed copy or
initial notification wave is implied. There is no full-query/role table or deferred-answer memo.
[run1-requests.md](run1-requests.md) defines the exact commit-then-replace barrier.

Preserve full source/sink NNF, F74/F75, D23, cleaner order, positive limits and hand-offs.
F78 ignores E and FLOW mark exclusions only for request matching/propagation. Ordinary
fact/summary/record operations retain them. Static inputs use the explicit field/class
partition and untouched frame; unrestricted raw root rows cannot bypass it. A request
is neither concrete evidence nor confirmation. The candidate and zero-GEN caveats of
§4.9 remain.

### 0.4 Run-1 all contributing origins (selected 21 October)

The [implementation contract](../docs/design/bidirectional-run1-origins-routing-projection-implementation-20261021.md)
replaces representative selection. For each accepted complete binding with
reference ND result `{I1, ..., Ik} -> Y`, emit `Ij -> Y` for every distinct
nonzero contributing original `Ij`. The result AP, mark, tail, exclusions
and effective layer stay unchanged. GROUP results remain DEMAND. An ordinary
atomic edge does not imply `Layer.NORMAL`. This rule takes precedence over
exact union in §§4.6, 7.1 and 8.9 **only in run-1**. Later FULL forward runs
keep complete ND premises, exact unions and E6.

This correction changes the representative runtime's semantic candidates
and demand relation. It can add caller/static candidates. It is not an
allocation-only optimization. Routing and projection optimizations must be
equivalent to this corrected all-origin reference, not the old representative
runtime. Field transfer, mark policy, cleaners, request barriers and the run
schedule do not change.

Require a complete compatible branch of the existing NNF predicate before
emission. Keep its proof, OR choices, repeated-leaf compatibility, all
contribution layers and the existing action/seed permission. A sink still
requires its whole condition and retains all checked literal inputs and
its proof. Never turn these into partial per-origin sink witnesses.

ZERO is precise. Emit a ZERO arm **if and only if** at least one accepted
complete compatible binding uses ZERO for every required input and passes
its existing action/seed permission. `{ZERO,I} -> Y` emits `I -> Y` and no
ZERO arm. ZERO choices pooled across different OR branches or incompatible
headers cannot admit a ZERO result. Keep the existing unconditional GEN
path. A request alone cannot satisfy a literal or create a ZERO source.

Each executable run-1 method edge, point resume, subscription and summary
still has one canonical `InitialAp` premise, including canonical ZERO. Use
the original initial, not the checked current fact or condition pattern.
Do not build a `PremiseSet` before splitting. Unary transfers retain their
original. Ordinary singleton call application retains its caller original.
Run-1 never enters E6 or publishes executable ND. Keep `ApManager.union`
and later FULL exact union unchanged.

The two local **result** stores factor accepted origin domains by proof and
compatible full facts header. Keep explicit conjunction slots distinct.
At shared canonical NNF leaves, require the same header and intersect origin
domains. Keep OR proof choices distinct. Do not expand NNF to cubes or
construct Cartesian origin products. A root publishes newly contributing
nonzero origins and independently publishes a newly permitted all-ZERO arm.
Same-header fact growth retains the existing union operation. Versions change
only for genuine growth; duplicate/stale visits emit no new arm. Freeze
releases the method-local state. Full sink binding evidence uses its separate
complete-binding path. The implementation contract states the store adapters.

Source transfer classification is unchanged. A completed MULTI source still
constructs its fixed target and uses its existing permission even when it
emits one atomic arm. Preserve unary/GEN geometry, action/occurrence IDs and
original source anchors/Facts. Do not reset a conditional source to ZERO.
Each nonstatic arm follows ordinary call matching. Each static arm follows
the existing actual pool matcher independently. A later caller can match
one arm without the other origins; added candidates stay under the existing
DEMAND policy. A complete reference caller binding can match every arm.
No omitted-support history or new grounding mechanism is added.

Handoff retains **full demand pairs**, including both entry and exit. For a
fixed accepted result with nonzero origins:

```text
H({I1,...,Ik} -> Y) = {(demand(Y), demand(Ij)) | j=1..k}
H({I1 -> Y,...,Ik -> Y}) = the same set of full pairs
```

The canonical all-ZERO result retains its ordinary explicit control-ZERO
exit. Both sides use the same conclusion/initial normalization and existing
merge/subsumption. Equal entry sets alone do not prove this law. Keep actual
query admission, entry-based additional guide emission, original FULL source
reversal, internal-sink seeds and ZERO discovery. Full pairs for corresponding
outputs do not by themselves prove whole-analyzer discovery or convergence.

[Run1AllOrigins.lean](lean/ApSpec/Run1AllOrigins.lean) proves exact scalar
origin/ZERO admission, factored independent-domain equality, repeated-leaf
intersection, complete handoff-pair equality and fresh-origin deltas.
[Run1RoutingProjection.lean](lean/ApSpec/Run1RoutingProjection.lean) proves
exact-class/descendant disjointness, prefix completeness, removed empty
effects and projection value idempotence. Their
[focused audit](lean/run1-origins-routing-projection-audit.lean) has 26
statements and 20 executable controls. The
[proof map](grouped-run1-statics-proofs.md#selected-21-october-all-origin-correction)
separates these local laws from production adapter and whole-engine claims.
Historical representative-only laws prove neither all-origin emission nor
full handoff-pair preservation. Atomic keys do not bound all AP work or time.

## 1. Terms

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| base; static base `S` | A local, argument, receiver, return, exception, constant, static/global base, or zero. `S` holds static fields and globals. |
| accessor; path | An `AccessorIdx`: a field, element `[e]`, or class/global accessor. A path is a list of concrete accessors. |
| root; root path | An entry method of the analysis; the empty path `[]` of a base. These are different uses of “root”. |
| tail; tail kind | `$`, `*`, may `[any]`, or must `[any-taint]`, together with its field exclusion (§2). |

## 2. The fact and the edge (the concept)

### 2.1 The tuple

A fact is `(base, path, tail, exclusion, mark)`:

* `path` — the concrete accessors. It never contains `[any]`, `[any-taint]`, a mark or `$`.
* `tail ∈ {*, [any], [any-taint], $}`. The `[any-taint]` tail has a concrete mark, and it occurs only in a forward
  run (W8).
* `exclusion` — a finite set of accessors, only with the `*` tail or the `[any-taint]` tail (W8).
* `mark ∈ {*, T}` for a premise; `mark ∈ {*, T, *∖X}` for a conclusion.

### 2.2 Edges, layers, the edge exclusion and the mark exclusion

An edge is `(premise set, layer) → (statement, conclusion)`. A fact-to-fact edge is also written
`(premise, layer) → (statement, conclusion)`. The zero-to-fact edge is `Zero → (layer, statement, fact)`: its premise
set is `{zero}`. An ND edge is `({premise1, …, premisek}, layer) → (statement, conclusion)` with `k ≥ 2` premises that
are not the zero fact (§4.6).

* An edge has ONE exclusion `E`. In a CORRELATED edge (`*` premise, `*` conclusion) the premise and the conclusion
  share it: for `(x, p, *) →_E (y, q, *)`, the value at `x.p.σ` flows to `y.q.σ` for every `σ` that `E` admits. The
  model stores `E` on the conclusion (the tail kind `*/E` of the target). If the premise also stores an exclusion, the
  edge exclusion is the union of the two (`SharedExcl.applyEdge_shared_excl`, `den_shared_excl`). An implementation
  stores `E` once, on the edge.
* An UNCORRELATED edge (the conclusion is `$` or has an any tail) has no shared exclusion. Its conclusion has the
  Empty exclusion, except an `[any-taint]/E` conclusion (W8): there `E` restricts the continuation of the conclusion
  only (§3.1). Every operation of §4 gives an uncorrelated result the Empty exclusion, except the rows of §4.1, §4.7
  and §6.3 that give an `[any-taint]` result its exclusion. An above-case transfer of a correlated fact loses its
  correlation and gives a demand result (§4.1). A `*/E` premise of an uncorrelated edge (before F72 a restricted
  run could emit one with a concrete mark, §6.3) keeps `E` in its premise: `E` restricts the premise continuation only. The
  exclusion of a must-premise (§6.3) does the same.
* The MARK EXCLUSION `X` of a conclusion `*∖X` stops the marks of `X`: the value at the premise location flows to the
  conclusion location only if its mark is not in `X`. It belongs to the edge, as the exclusion does; a cleaner makes it
  (§4.7). A premise never has one.
* The policy facts and the chain answers of run 1 have the Empty exclusion (`Reverse.policy_premEmpty`,
  `Reverse.answerInit_premEmpty`). A catalog structural initial `(S, p, *, {}, *)` has the Empty exclusion by its definition
  (F78 §4.10; historical scalar position answers have the same Empty E). F78 static answers use the supplied field projector and direct class path. They have a concrete
  mark and the `$` or chain `*` tail, all with Empty E. An exact field leaf gives `$`;
  a nonexact `[any]`/`[any-taint]` leaf or broad ancestor gives the chain `*` answer.
  No run-1 InitialAp has `[any]` or `[any-taint]`; its incoming/starting fact may have an any tail.
  The exhaustive ten-family initial grammar is F78 §1.1.
  (The Lean theorems above do not cover all these static answers; the
  statements follow from their definitions.) In a restricted run an emitted fact can have the exclusion of the demand.
  Before F72 it was the meet with a `*/E` entry pattern (§6.3), with a concrete mark, so it started in the demand
  layer (§6.5) and made no record. Since F72 a `*/E` entry pattern has the mark `*` (W2), so it gives its FLOW form
  `(x, p, */E, *)` (§6.3): it starts with the identity in the normal layer (§6.5), as a policy fact does, and its
  exclusion is the shared exclusion of its correlated edges (above). (In the spec runs no demand pattern has the tail
  `*/E`: every `*` pattern has the entry tail `[any]`, and its FLOW form `*/{}` has the Empty exclusion, §6.3.) A
  must-premise of a forward restricted run can
  have the exclusion of its `[any-taint]/E` added fact (§6.3); it starts in the normal layer with it (§6.5). So the
  exclusion of a normal edge is a property of its conclusion (and of a must-premise). Only a strong field write makes
  it larger (by its keep edge, or through a `*/E` summary or record), and, on an `[any-taint]` fact, a cleaner one
  accessor below it (§4.7).
* The LAYER is part of the edge identity. A micro edge has no layer (§4.2): the layer belongs to the propagation edge.
  Only these AP operations put a propagation edge in the demand layer:
  * in selected run 1, only a surviving E-requiring residual of a static/nonstatic
    field write or other operation takes an E-free DEMAND cover; complete
    overwrite kills and disjoint preservation remain. Also application
    of an ordinary DEMAND default static summary ([phase contract](run1-field-writes.md));
  * the start fact of an initial fact with the `[any]` tail (historical/restricted initials), or with the `*` tail and a concrete mark (§6.5). F78 run 1 uses only the latter nonexact initial. An
    `[any-taint]` start fact (a must-premise, forward restricted runs only) is normal;
  * the case `above` of §4.1 for a fact that is not `[any-taint]`;
  * an `[any]` result (W6: a may), and the concrete-STAR payload projector (§4.1 step 6);
  * in the backward run, every result of the reversal of a micro edge whose forward target is `[any]` (a pass rule
    with an `AnyField` target, a may), also a `$` result (§9.1);
  * the cut of the field limit (§4.4);
  * a conjunction with an input that is in the demand layer, or that its literal does not cover and that is not
    `[any-taint]` (§4.6);
  * the application of a demand-layer summary edge (§4.3), also of a summary with several premises (§4.6); the
    application of a must record by `applicable` only (§4.3);
  * the `part` rows of the cleaner that give a demand-layer result (§4.7);
  * the END FACTS of a sink (§4.9): an end-fact edge takes no input fact. When a sink edge triggers, or a conjunctive
    sink completes a combination, it applies to the zero fact in the layer of that sink edge or of that combination
    (a combination is in the demand layer if one of its edges is).

  A demand-layer input gives a demand-layer result. The layer of an edge never goes back to normal
  (`Invariant.applyEdge_demand_monotone` and the related lemmas). On an `[any-taint]` fact only these operations give
  a demand-layer result. A layer-only change retains its known tail and E; an
  actual information-losing transfer has its own shape rule (THE DEMOTIONS; the other lists of this spec
  refer to this one): the field-limit cut (§4.4); a cleaner `part` row of §4.7 other than the `atAndBelow` and `below`
  rows one accessor below the fact (so the `exact` cleaner at the path of the fact or one accessor below it, and every
  cleaner two or more accessors below it); a may target (an `[any]` target of a pass rule, W6); a demand input (a
  demand fact, summary edge or record: another input of a conjunction in the demand layer, §4.6, a demand-layer
  summary edge or record, §4.3, or a demand link, an `[any]` added fact, §4.3); and the must-record demotion
  (§4.3; Lean `AnyTaint.recLayer`, `AnyTaintEx.recLayerX`). An exclusion that meets an `[any-taint]` fact (the keep
  edge of a strong write, a `*/E` summary or record) does NOT give a demand result: the result keeps the layer and
  carries the exclusion (W8 (a); §4.1).

Lean: `PFact` (a premise or a conclusion; the conclusion `*/E` carries the exclusion of the edge; the mark is `MarkA`
with `star`, `conc t`, `starEx x`) and `AFact` (a conclusion plus `demand : Bool`, the layer); with the exclusion of
`[any-taint]`, `AnyTaintEx.XFact` (an `AFact` plus its exclusion `ex`).

### 2.3 Well-formedness rules

Selected run-1 specialization: **all field E is Empty**, on every intermediate
fact and both summary payloads, including source-generated must facts.
Complete overwrite kills remain kills in either layer; disjoint components
remain unchanged. Only a surviving E-requiring residual takes a DEMAND cover. Layer demotion itself
preserves the full AP payload, including STAR or ANY_TAINT; it does not create
ANY. The older demand-driven normalizers below and their Lean theorems describe
the prior contract. They do not prove the selected layer-only rule. Later
strong field operations retain their ordinary exclusions.

| Rule | Text |
|---|---|
| W1 | An edge with no `*` side has the Empty exclusion. |
| W2 | A conclusion with the `*` tail has the mark `*` or `*∖X`. The layer is independent: moving a known STAR edge to DEMAND retains STAR. A premise may have the `*` tail with a concrete mark (a request answer in run 1; before F72 also, in a restricted run, the meet of an added fact with a `*/E` entry pattern, which F72 replaces by the FLOW form, §6.3). |
| W3 | In a run with the field limit `L`, every result of an operation has at most `L` counted accessors (§4.4). This claim needs nondecreasing limits (§6.6), bounded seeds, and binding-in edges that do not increase the counted path depth. The interpreter bindings into a callee meet this condition (`interpreter.md` §3.1). Then an added fact, a premise emitted from a demand chain (§6.3), and a fact on an untouched base stay in the bound. A generic micro edge (§4.2) has no bound; nondecreasing limits alone do not bound a path-growing binding (`ReviewDemand.binding_in_needs_non_growth_condition`). W3 as a whole is argued, not proved (§11.2). |
| W4 | `[any]` and `[any-taint]` are tails only. A path has no inner `[any]` or `[any-taint]`. |
| W5 | Marks are not accessors. `TaintMarkAccessor`, `FinalAccessor` and `AnyAccessor` do not occur in a path. `TypeInfoAccessor`, `TypeInfoGroupAccessor` and `ValueAccessor` do not occur either: the type-info accessors serve only the lambda analysis of the prescan, and no statement and no rule makes a value accessor. |
| W6 | A conclusion with the `[any]` tail is in the demand layer. |
| W7 | Only a conclusion has a mark exclusion. An edge whose premise set has two or more members (an ND edge, §4.6) has no `*` tail. |
| W8 | THE `[any-taint]` RULE. (a) `[any-taint]` has a concrete mark only (never `*` or `*∖X`). It is a TAINT conclusion (§7.2). It can carry an EXCLUSION `E` of first accessors (`[any-taint]/E`, §1). A conclusion or must-premise can retain its spatial exclusion independently of layer; all run-1 exclusions are Empty by the phase contract. `[any]` and `$` have Empty E. The earlier `AnyTaintEx.carriesB`/`normX` laws describe the older layer-coupled representation. (b) LAYER INDEPENDENCE: a DEMAND edge can retain an `[any-taint]` conclusion. Demotion alone changes neither tail nor E. A transfer which actually loses information can produce `[any]`; an explicit run-1 E-free cover can forget E. Neither is inferred merely from DEMAND. (c) An `[any-taint]` PREMISE (a must-premise) occurs only in a forward restricted run, never in run 1 (§6.5). (d) `[any-taint]` is a FORWARD tail. The backward run has no fact, premise, edge or demand pattern with the `[any-taint]` tail: its seeds and its reversed `[any]` literals give `[any]` (§9.1, §9.2), and the hand-off reads a forward `[any-taint]/E` conclusion as the pattern `[any]` (§9.2). A normal edge with the `[any-taint]` tail is complete (§1). |

W2 holds for every derived fact, in run 1 without the static rule and the conjunctions (the closure `D`:

They have the mark `*` or `*∖X` and are in the normal layer, so W2 holds for them for the same reason as in run 1

### 2.4 The zero fact

The zero fact is `(zero, [], $, {}, zeroMark)`. Its one location is the zero location. An unconditional source rule
is a micro edge from the zero fact (a conditional source reads another fact, `interpreter.md` §4.1). The zero fact is
a premise like every other initial fact: a zero-to-fact edge is an edge with the premise set `{zero}`, in the normal or
the demand layer. A conjunction drops the zero fact from the union of its premise sets (§4.6). The cases where an
operation treats the zero fact in a special way:

* the statement transfer (§4.2) and the call (§3.5, §5.3): the zero fact passes, and it enters every resolved callee;
* the conjunction (§4.6): the union of the premise sets drops the zero fact;
* the cleaner (§4.7) and the type filter (§4.8): no cleaner is on the zero base, and a type filter on the zero base
  accepts the empty path (S11 (d));
* the sink check (§4.9): an unconditional sink triggers on the zero fact; the premise set `{zero}` is supported at a
  root and through the zero edges of the callers;
* the run-1 abstraction (§6.2), the emission (§6.3) and the start fact (§6.5): the zero fact gives the zero fact;
* the backward run (§9.2): the zero rules.

## 3. Denotation

### 3.1 Admitted continuations

`E.admits σ` is true if `σ = []`, or if the first accessor of `σ` is not in `E`.

| Tail | As a premise, the continuations `σ` that it covers | As a conclusion, the relation of the premise continuation `σ` to its own continuation `τ` |
|---|---|---|
| `*/E` | all `σ` that `E` admits | `τ = σ` and `E` admits `σ` (CORRELATED) |
| `[any]` | all `σ` | any `τ` (not correlated) |
| `[any-taint]/E` | all `σ` that `E` admits | any `τ` that `E` admits (not correlated) |
| `$` | `σ = []` | `τ = []` |

`[any-taint]` with the Empty exclusion has the denotation of `[any]`. Its exclusion `E` removes the continuations that
start with an accessor of `E`: on a premise it restricts `σ`, on a conclusion `τ`. It is not shared: the edge stays
uncorrelated. The layer gives the reading (W6, W8): a normal `[any-taint]/E` conclusion is exact (end-exact for a
must-premise, §1), so EVERY admitted location at or below its path carries the mark (a must); a demand `[any]`
conclusion over-approximates (a may). An `[any-taint]/E` premise covers the `σ` that `E` admits: its edges hold when
every admitted location of it carries the mark (a must-premise, §1). Lean: `AnyTaintEx.coversX` (a premise),
`coversFX` (a conclusion), `denX` (an edge).

### 3.2 Location set and edge relation

```
covers(i, l)  ⇔  l.base = i.base ∧ l.path = i.path ++ σ ∧ σ admitted by i.tail ∧ i.mark admits l.mark

den(i, f)(l0, l1)  ⇔  l0.base = i.base ∧ l1.base = f.base
                    ∧ i.mark admits l0.mark ∧ l1.mark = out(f.mark, l0.mark) ∧ f.mark passes l0.mark
                    ∧ ∃ σ τ. l0.path = i.path ++ σ ∧ l1.path = f.path ++ τ
                             ∧ σ admitted by i.tail ∧ (σ, τ) related by f.tail
```

with `admits(*, m)`, `admits(T, m) ⇔ m = T`, `admits(*∖X, m) ⇔ m ∉ X`, `out(*, m) = out(*∖X, m) = m`,
`out(T, m) = T`, and `passes(*∖X, m) ⇔ m ∉ X` (true for the other marks).

`den(i, f)(l0, l1)` reads: "the value at `l0` on method entry flows to `l1` at the statement of the edge". Lean:
`PFact.covers`, `den`, `MarkA.admits`, `MarkA.passes`. The tail of an `[any-taint]/E` side admits only what `E`
admits (§3.1; Lean: `AnyTaintEx.coversX`, `denX`).

Derived relations:

* `i` COVERS the fact `c` if every location of `c` is a location of `i` (Lean: `coversB`). It compares the marks: the
  marks of `c` must be a subset of the marks of `i` (Lean: `markSubB`).
* Two facts OVERLAP if they have a common location with the marks ignored (Lean: `overlapB`; with the exclusion of an
  `[any-taint]/E` fact, `AnyTaintEx.overlapX`). Every overlap test of this spec ignores the marks: the request match
  (§4.5), the conjunction store (§4.6), the sink check (§4.9) and the restriction (§6.4). Each of these places tests
  the marks separately. Each one reads the exclusion of an `[any-taint]/E` fact as part of its location set: an
  excluded location overlaps nothing.
* The restriction reads a demand pattern WITH ITS MARKS (§6.4; `ap-history.md` F71): the premise must lie inside `D-c`
  in its locations and in its marks (Lean: `Handoff.insideB`), and the mark of the conclusion must meet the mark of
  `D-p` (`Handoff.concMarkB`). The emission reads the entry pattern with its mark (`markMatchB`, §6.3; a `*∖X` entry
  pattern does not admit a mark of `X`; since F72 no pattern has the mark `*∖X`: the hand-off replaces it by `*`,
  §9.2). The demanded flows read both patterns with their marks (`PFact.covers`, §1).

### 3.3 Exclusion algebra and merge rules

* The edge exclusion is the union of what the model stores on the two sides (`SharedExcl.applyEdge_shared_excl`).
* MERGE RULE 1: two edges with the same premise, the same layer, the same exclusion and the same mark exclusion merge
  their conclusions (union).
* MERGE RULE 2: two edges with the same premise, the same layer and the same conclusion merge their exclusions by
  INTERSECTION: `admits(E1 ∩ E2, σ) = admits(E1, σ) ∨ admits(E2, σ)`. The union of the two relations is exact
  (`Subsume.merge_inter`). Two `[any-taint]/E1` and `[any-taint]/E2` conclusions with the same premise, layer, path
  and mark merge in the same way, into `[any-taint]/(E1 ∩ E2)` (argued, §11.2: the model has no merge rule for the
  exclusion of `[any-taint]`).
* MERGE RULE 2 FOR MARKS: two edges with the same premise, layer, exclusion and conclusion but mark exclusions `X1`, `X2`
  merge into one with `X1 ∩ X2`: a mark passes the merged edge if and only if it passes one of them
  (`Tree.rule2_mark`).
* A UNION of exclusions happens only along one derivation (a field write after another, a cleaner after another). A
  union across two different edges is FORBIDDEN: it removes pairs that one of the two edges has
  (`Subsume.union_loses_pairs`).

### 3.4 Reference types and tests

The reference forms of §4 and §6 use these types. A premise, a pattern and an added fact are a `Pattern`: a path fact
with the exclusion of its `*` tail or of its `[any-taint]` tail (W8). The implementation interns a premise as an
`InitialAp` (§7.1).

```kotlin
/** ANY is `[any]` (a may), ANY_TAINT is `[any-taint]` (a must, W8; forward runs only). ANY_TAINT can carry an
 *  exclusion; with the Empty exclusion the two have the same location set (§3.1). */
enum class Tail { STAR, ANY, ANY_TAINT, EXACT }

/** An any tail: `[any]` or `[any-taint]`. */
val Tail.isAny: Boolean get() = this == Tail.ANY || this == Tail.ANY_TAINT

/** A canonical (sorted, de-duplicated) set of concrete marks: the X of *∖X. Operations: `in`, `isSubsetOf`, `+`. */
class MarkSet(val ids: IntArray) {
    companion object { val EMPTY = MarkSet(IntArray(0)) }
}

/** A finite set of accessors: the exclusion E. Empty, or Concrete with a canonical non-empty set. No Universe (§1). */
sealed interface ExclusionSet {
    data object Empty : ExclusionSet
    class Concrete(val ids: IntArray) : ExclusionSet            // sorted, de-duplicated AccessorIdx, never empty
    fun admits(r: List<Accessor>): Boolean                     // r = [] or the first accessor of r is not in the set
    fun union(other: ExclusionSet): ExclusionSet
    fun isSubsetOf(other: ExclusionSet): Boolean
}

/** `p` is a prefix of this list. */
fun <T> List<T>.startsWith(p: List<T>): Boolean = size >= p.size && subList(0, p.size) == p

/** The static base S (`ClassStatic`, §4.10). */
val STATIC: AccessPathBase = AccessPathBase.ClassStatic

/** `*` is Star(MarkSet.EMPTY). A premise never has excluded marks. Since F72 a demand pattern never has them either:
 *  the hand-off replaces `*∖X` by `*` (§9.2). (Under F71 an entry pattern from a run-1 summary conclusion kept them,
 *  and the emission and the restriction read them exactly, §6.3, §6.4.) An added fact and a conclusion can have
 *  them. */
sealed interface MarkSlot {
    data class Star(val excluded: MarkSet) : MarkSlot     // *  or  *∖X
    data class Concrete(val mark: TaintMark) : MarkSlot   // T; the zero mark is a concrete mark
}

data class PathFact(val base: AccessPathBase, val path: List<Accessor>, val tail: Tail, val mark: MarkSlot)

/** A premise, a demand pattern or an added fact: a fact with its own exclusion (Empty unless the tail is STAR, or
 *  ANY_TAINT in a forward run: the exclusion of `[any-taint]/E`, W8). */
data class Pattern(val fact: PathFact, val exclusion: ExclusionSet)

/** A demand pattern (§1): the entry pattern D-c and the exit pattern D-p (null: the demand does not reach the exit). */
data class DemandPattern(val entry: Pattern, val exit: Pattern?)

/** §3.1: the tail admits the continuation r. */
fun tailAdmits(tail: Tail, exclusion: ExclusionSet, r: List<Accessor>): Boolean = when (tail) {
    Tail.STAR, Tail.ANY_TAINT -> exclusion.admits(r)   // r = [] or the first accessor of r is not excluded
    Tail.ANY -> true
    Tail.EXACT -> r.isEmpty()
}
fun Pattern.tailAdmits(r: List<Accessor>) = tailAdmits(fact.tail, exclusion, r)

/** The marks of `c` are a subset of the marks of `i` (Lean: markSubB). */
fun markSub(i: MarkSlot, c: MarkSlot): Boolean = when (i) {
    is MarkSlot.Star -> when (c) {
        is MarkSlot.Star -> i.excluded.isSubsetOf(c.excluded)   // *∖X ⊇ *∖Y if and only if X ⊆ Y; * ⊇ every abstract mark
        is MarkSlot.Concrete -> c.mark !in i.excluded
    }
    is MarkSlot.Concrete -> c is MarkSlot.Concrete && c.mark == i.mark
}

/** Tail inclusion at the same path: every continuation of c is a continuation of i (Lean: tailSubB). */
private fun tailSub(i: Pattern, c: Pattern): Boolean = when (i.fact.tail) {
    Tail.ANY -> true
    Tail.EXACT -> c.fact.tail == Tail.EXACT
    Tail.STAR, Tail.ANY_TAINT -> when (c.fact.tail) {       // the exclusion of i must exclude only what c excludes
        Tail.EXACT -> true
        Tail.ANY -> i.exclusion == ExclusionSet.Empty
        Tail.STAR, Tail.ANY_TAINT -> i.exclusion.isSubsetOf(c.exclusion)
    }
}

/** `i` covers every location of `c`, marks included (Lean: coversB). */
fun covers(i: Pattern, c: Pattern): Boolean {
    if (i.fact.base != c.fact.base || !markSub(i.fact.mark, c.fact.mark)) return false
    val p = i.fact.path
    val q = c.fact.path
    if (!q.startsWith(p)) return false
    return if (q.size == p.size) tailSub(i, c) else i.tailAdmits(q.drop(p.size))
}

/** A common location, marks ignored (Lean: overlapB). */
fun overlap(a: Pattern, b: Pattern): Boolean {
    if (a.fact.base != b.fact.base) return false
    val p = a.fact.path
    val q = b.fact.path
    return when {
        q.startsWith(p) -> a.tailAdmits(q.drop(p.size))
        p.startsWith(q) -> b.tailAdmits(p.drop(q.size))
        else -> false
    }
}

/** §4.3, run 1; a record also in every later run (with inside, R4): the premise j covers the added fact a
 *  (Lean: applicable). A premise with an any tail needs a fact with an any tail. F78 run 1 has no `[any]` or `[any-taint]`
 *  premise; a must record that applies by applicable only gives a demand result (§4.3). */
fun applicable(j: Pattern, a: Pattern): Boolean =
    covers(j, a) && (!j.fact.tail.isAny || a.fact.tail.isAny)

/** §4.3, the summaries of a restricted run: j lies inside a as locations, and markSub(j, a) (Lean: satI; with the
 *  exclusions of `[any-taint]/E` facts and premises AnyTaintEx.satX). A normal result of a must-premise (an
 *  `[any-taint]` j) needs this test (Lean: SatInsideX). Since F72 a FLOW premise (the mark `*`) also applies by
 *  applicable (§4.3; `satisfies` of §6.3). */
fun inside(j: Pattern, a: Pattern): Boolean =
    covers(a.copy(fact = a.fact.copy(mark = MarkSlot.Star(MarkSet.EMPTY))), j) && markSub(j.fact.mark, a.fact.mark)
```

An empty Concrete `ExclusionSet` must not exist (return `Empty`). `Accessor` is an interned accessor, and
`AccessorIdx` is its intern id (the accessor interning of today, §7.6): `admits(r)` reads the `AccessorIdx` of the
first accessor of `r` and tests it against `ids`. Keep the excluded accessors as a CANONICAL (sorted, de-duplicated)
`IntArray` of `AccessorIdx`; the same for `MarkSet`. The edge trees are keyed by both, so two equal sets
must be equal values. Because the sets of accessors and marks are unbounded (§1), these tests are exact: `covers`,
`overlap` and `cleanPos` (§4.7) need no "all accessors" or "all marks" case. The tests read `ANY_TAINT` with its
exclusion as a location set, as `*/E` reads its exclusion: with the Empty exclusion it is `ANY` (§3.1). So `covers`,
`overlap`, `applicable` and `inside` read the exclusion of an `[any-taint]/E` fact or premise (Lean:
`AnyTaintEx.coversX`, `overlapX`, `satX`). The operations that read the difference of the two any tails (the layer)
say so (§4.1, §4.3, §4.6, §4.9, §6.3).

### 3.5 Concrete semantics

The theorems compare the analysis with this semantics. It is the program that the micro edges describe (S1). It is
alias-free and location-level. Lean: `Basic.lean` (`Stmt.step`, `Flow`, `Reach`). `Flow` is this semantics without
the override of the summary rewriter (REFERENCE SEMANTICS OF RULES, below).

* STATEMENT STEP. A statement with the touched bases `B` and the micro edges `M` moves the location `l` to `l'` if
  `l.base` is not in `B` and `l' = l`, or if a micro edge `e` of `M` relates them: `den(e)(l, l')` (§3.2). So an
  untouched base keeps its locations, and a touched base keeps only what a micro edge gives.
* CLEANER STEP. A cleaner `(x, p, reach, mark)` (§4.7) removes the location `l` if `l.base = x`, the cleaner removes
  the mark of `l` (its own mark, or every mark), and `l.path = p ++ σ` with `σ` in the reach: `exact`: `σ = []`;
  `below`: `σ ≠ []`; `atAndBelow`: every `σ`. Every other location passes unchanged (Lean: `Cleaner.cleansB`).
* FILTER STEP. A type filter `filter(b, may)` (§4.8) removes a location on the base `b` whose path `may` rejects. Every
  other location passes unchanged.
* CALL STEP. A call has the touched caller bases, the binding edges into the callee and the binding edges back. A
  caller location on an untouched base passes over the call. A location `l` on a touched base goes into the callee
  through a binding edge `e1` (`den(e1)(l, l1)`), flows in the callee from the entry location `l1` to an exit location
  `l2`, and comes back through a binding edge back `e2` (`den(e2)(l2, l3)`) as `l3`. For the call `r = m(a1..an)` the
  touched caller bases are the arguments, the result and the static base; the bindings into the callee are
  `ai.* → argi.*`, `S.* → S.*` and `zero.* → zero.*`; the bindings back are `argi.* → ai.*`, `ret.* → r.*` and
  `S.* → S.*`. The interpreter gives the bindings of each call kind (`interpreter.md` §3). The zero base is never a
  touched base of a call: the zero location passes over every call, and it also enters the callee through
  `zero.* → zero.*`. A binding has the premise mark `*` (S10), so the zero binding has the `*` form, and the zero fact
  is at or below its premise. Lean: `Call`, `Flow.pass`, `Flow.call`.
* FLOW. A flow of the method `M` from the entry location `l0` is a chain of these steps from the entry node of `M` to a
  node `n`. It ends at the location `l`: the value at `l0` on method entry is at `l` at `n` (Lean: `Flow`). A call step
  contains the flow of the callee.
* VULNERABILITY AND WITNESS. A sink pattern `s` with the concrete mark `T` at the node `n` is REACHED if the zero
  location of a root flows to a location at `n` that `s` covers. The flow can go down into callees: from a location at a
  call node, through a binding edge into the callee, then a flow in the callee (Lean: `Reach`). Such a chain is a
  WITNESS of the vulnerability. A vulnerability is REAL if it has a witness.
* REFERENCE SEMANTICS OF RULES. The interpreter rules are read in this semantics as follows (S1). First fold signed source/sink conditions before and after static evaluation (`interpreter.md` §4.2).
  An eligible residual negative literal then counts as true. A signed contradiction is false and has no effect. A pass rule has no mark literal (a pass rule with a mark literal is a
  rule error that is not rejected, `interpreter.md` §1.3: it fires without its mark literals, §11.1). A user-defined
  rule that the summary rewriter selects REPLACES the callee flow for its marks at its positions (§4.7). The override
  is not in `Flow`. The theorems read the program in which each call with selected rules is wrapped: the callee flow,
  then the cleaner `(P, exact, T)` for each selected rule, mark and position (for an `AnyField` position
  `(P, atAndBelow, T)` for a source, `(P, below, T)` for a cleaner, §4.7), on the callee results; the source
  results and the end facts of the call bypass the wrapper (argued, §11.2). An end-fact action is a source at its
  sink statement that fires when its sink fires (§4.9). The model has none (§11.2). A micro edge with an any target
  gives the value of its premise location to EVERY location at or below its target path (§3.2). For a source with an
  `[any]` target this is the rule itself (a must, S15). For a pass rule with an `AnyField` target it over-approximates
  the callee, which writes some field: W6 keeps its results in the demand layer (§2.3), and the backward run keeps
  every result of its reversal in the demand layer (§9.1). A conjunction of literals on
  different facts is path-insensitive: each literal can hold on its own path. Its semantics is the SUPPORT semantics: a location is tainted
  at a node together with the list of entry locations that its derivation needs, and a vulnerability witness is a tree
  (§4.6; Lean: `ND.TaintN`, `ND.ReachAll`). "Real" in this spec always means real in this reference semantics.
